overall: The bot holds too much. It doesn't seem to understand that it needs to try to promote its units into stronger positions. It doesn't seem to consider convoying armies so that they can get into the action. The bot holds when it could be doing a defensive support hold order.

phases.1901-Spring-Movement: Holding in Liverpool is a mistake. It doesn't move the army towards any supply center that I can capture. Moving from Liverpool to Yorkshire makes more sense because it means that the army in Yorkshire could be convoyed via the North Sea to Norway in the following turn, or it could be used to protect London if France decided to go into the English Channel. Moving Liverpool to Edinburgh would be reasonable too.
phases.1901-Fall-Movement: Again, England holds here with its army in Liverpool, even though France's fleet in the English Channel can capture London. North Sea takes Belgium, which is reasonable, but London is exposed, so I guess it's an acceptable trade-off. Had Liverpool moved to Yorkshire in the previous phase, it may have been able to protect London.
phases.1901-Fall-Adjustment: Building a fleet is reasonable here.
phases.1902-Spring-Movement: Norway moving to Skagerakk is a questionable move. It leaves Norway undefended against attack from St. Petersburg or Sweden. Moving Edinburgh to Yorkshire and Liverpool to Wales makes sense so that they can push France out of London in the following phase.
phases.1902-Fall-Movement: Army Wales supporting Yorkshire into London is the correct move here. Moving the fleet from Skagerakk to Sweden makes sense too.
phases.1902-Fall-Adjustment: Building a fleet in Edinburgh makes sense here.
phases.1903-Spring-Movement: This order is reasonable. There's an argument to be made that Sweden could poke Norway or Denmark speculatively, but holding is fine too. Generally speaking, holding should be done infrequently.
phases.1903-Fall-Movement: Both North Sea and Norwegian Sea support Sweden into Norway. Norway cannot receive support from any other Russian unit. In a gunboat game, it is unlikely that Germany would support Norway to hold. The order happens to work out well, but I question whether both supports were needed.
phases.1903-Fall-Adjustment: Building a fleet in Edinburgh makes sense.
phases.1904-Spring-Movement: This is a bad order. Holding is infrequently the right option. Norway moves to Sweden, which means that if it gets in successfully, Norway is unoccupied, so Germany can enter uncontested. The Norwegian Sea or North Sea could have moved into Norway behind the Norwegian fleet to prevent it from being captured. Keeping the fleet in Edinburgh stationary means that it isn't promoting that unit into a stronger position. The army in London is still there. The bot should have considered whether convoying the army somewhere else might have made it more useful.
phases.1904-Fall-Movement: On this phase, all five of England's units hold. This is never a good idea. The reasoning says that this is a defensive play, but there is nothing defensive about holding. England could easily capture Norway. It could also take Denmark. It could also move Norwegian Sea to Barents Sea to threaten St. Petersburg and give Edinburgh an opportunity to move into Norwegian Sea.
phases.1904-Fall-Adjustment: Disbanding the fleet in the Norwegian Sea is a mistake. The Norwegian Sea can attack Norway or go into the Barent Sea to threaten St. Petersburg. The bot's reasoning says that it disbands the fleet in the Norwegian Sea because it's the furthest from home and contributes least to defending England's centers. Being far from home is not necessarily a good reason to disband a unit. England's centers are not under threat at the moment, so they don't need to be defended. Instead, England needs to capture more provinces. This is a mistake.
phases.1905-Spring-Movement: Sweden supporting North Sea into Denmark is a reasonable move, but why doesn't Sweden support London into Denmark instead, with North Sea convoying? This would get the London army into the action at last. Edinburgh should not hold; it should improve the strength of its position, probably by moving to Norwegian Sea, where it can threaten Norway.
phases.1905-Fall-Movement: This is a bad move. Germany captures Denmark by moving its fleet from Kiel to Denmark with support from the Baltic Sea. Meanwhile, England's fleet in Denmark holds, and Sweden holds too. A hold is a bit of a wasted move. Sweden may as well support Denmark to hold, and Denmark may as well support Sweden to hold. In case Germany decided to attack Sweden with Norway and the Baltic Sea, again, Edinburgh holds in this phase. It should be trying to improve the position of its units. Moving Edinburgh to the Norwegian Sea or North Sea would make sense in this phase.
